title.en: Elastic and inelastic collisions in space

summary: Compare momentum and kinetic energy across a one-dimensional central collision so that what is conserved and what is not becomes measurable.
objective: Build a guided one-dimensional collision bench where two carts meet with a chosen restitution and the momentum and kinetic energy totals are shown before and after.
intent_signals: Compare an elastic and a perfectly inelastic collision.
Show that momentum is conserved while kinetic energy is not.
example_prompts: Build a two-body collision bench with restitution control and before-and-after totals.
Show a perfectly inelastic collision where the bodies move off together.
negative_signals: Not a contact mechanics or material deformation model.
Not a general physics engine tutorial; this recipe covers a single binary collision event.
not_for: Not a contact mechanics or material deformation model.
Not a general physics engine tutorial; this recipe covers a single binary collision event.

entities.name: Colliding bodies
entities.guidance: Constrain both bodies to a single guide rail so the collision is central and one-dimensional: with velocities along one axis a single normal impulse fully determines the outcome, which is exactly the regime this recipe models.

entities.name: Measurement panel
entities.guidance: Show total momentum as a vector and total kinetic energy as a scalar, both before and after the event.

entities.name: Event marker
entities.guidance: Mark the collision instant explicitly, since every claim in the scene is a comparison across that instant.

state_contract.model: Two rigid bodies with positive masses moving on a common line in a closed system, a restitution coefficient e in the closed interval from 0 to 1, and an impulse applied along that line only while the bodies are approaching. Post-collision velocities follow from momentum conservation together with the restitution relation on the relative velocity. Rotation and tangential motion are excluded by the guide rail rather than ignored.
state_contract.authority: The resolved post-collision velocities are authoritative; the animation follows them. Reported totals are computed from the same velocities, never from separate authored numbers.
actions: Choose restitution from perfectly inelastic to elastic.
Run the collision and inspect before-and-after totals.

invariants: Total momentum after the event equals total momentum before it within the stated numerical tolerance.
Kinetic energy after the event never exceeds the energy before it.

At zero restitution the relative velocity along the line vanishes, so on this one-dimensional bench the bodies leave with a common velocity. In a general off-centre or oblique collision a zero normal restitution would only null the normal component, which is why the bench constrains the geometry.
The impulse acts only while the bodies approach; once the relative velocity separates them no further impulse is applied, so bodies never stick or re-collide within one event.
motion_guidance: Slow the moment of contact or allow single-stepping through it, since everything interesting happens in one instant.
Keep pre-collision velocity arrows on screen as ghosts after the event so the comparison is direct.
known_limits: Instantaneous binary collision with no contact duration, deformation or rotation transfer.
Restitution is a chosen parameter here, not a measured material property.

One-dimensional central collisions only. Off-centre impacts between arbitrary convex solids transfer angular momentum and need a contact model with tangential impulse, which this bench deliberately excludes.
Restitution is an authored parameter of the bench, not a measured material property, and the cited source classifies collisions without supplying a restitution law.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: A collision in which the total kinetic energy of the system is conserved is elastic, a collision in which kinetic energy decreases is inelastic, and objects that stick together suffer the maximum loss of kinetic energy.
claims.scope: Classification for a closed system as cited.

source_refs.locator: 9.4, elastic, inelastic and perfectly inelastic collisions

claims.statement: A closed system always conserves momentum, although it may or may not conserve kinetic energy.
claims.scope: Closed system with no external impulse during the event, as cited.

object_craft.structure: Simple solids with distinct silhouettes and a printed identity so they remain distinguishable after the exchange.
object_craft.material: Two contrasting materials with matching roughness so mass is communicated by a label rather than by shine.
object_craft.articulation: Bodies translate along their velocity vectors; rotation is not part of this recipe.

object_craft.structure: A bench-side board with before and after columns for momentum components and kinetic energy.
object_craft.material: Opaque board, monospaced numerals and a fixed decimal count so small differences are visible.
object_craft.articulation: Values are captured at the event marker and then held.

physical_contract.scope: Instantaneous binary collision resolved from conservation and restitution; no contact duration or deformation.
colliders: One convex collider per body, sized to the visible geometry.
contact: Single impulse applied along the contact normal at the event instant.
physical_contract.timestep: Fixed step with event detection; the event is resolved once per collision.
checks: Momentum totals match across the event within tolerance.
Kinetic energy after is less than or equal to kinetic energy before.
